title: para = in order to, -ando in the past, no -ing as a subject, -ante / -iente, days of the week

cards.title: para = in order to
cards.body: When English 'to' means 'in order to', Spanish needs para; the 'to' form alone isn't enough.

examples.en: We've talked in order to resolve it.

cards.title: Learn from Spanish speakers' English
cards.body: 'I am here for see you' is negative transfer from Spanish. Mistakes you keep hearing often reveal the Spanish structure.

examples.en: I've called you to talk about it.

cards.title: Recap: estar + -ando / -iendo
cards.body: The little word can attach to the -ando form. Explicar comes from plicare, 'to fold': explaining is unfolding.

cards.title: Ongoing periods use -ing too
cards.body: 'I'm taking a course' covers an ongoing period. In the past, estaba + -ando and the line past are mostly interchangeable.

examples.es: Estoy tomando un curso de español.

examples.en: I was taking a Spanish course.
examples.es: Estaba tomando / Tomaba un curso de español.

cards.title: 'Swimming is healthy' = to swim is healthy
cards.body: Use the 'to' form as a subject. Salud (health) is also the word for 'cheers!'.

cards.title: Days of the week = planets
cards.body: Spanish shows the planets clearly: lunes (moon), martes (Mars), miércoles (Mercury), jueves (Jupiter), viernes (Venus).
